answer_1.quote: Radiology report generation is a task of generating reports comprising a sequence of sentences
answer_1.outputs: radiology reports describing medical image findings with factual accuracy and consistent description order

answer_2.quote: In addition to the NLG metrics, such as BLEU, BERTScore, and ROUGE (Lin, 2004), we deploy a clinical factual accuracy metric in and Content Ordering (CO) metric that quantifies the consistency of the description order of the reports.

answer_4.quote: Two experts for the JLiverCT and six experts for the MIMIC-CXR dataset who are knowledgeable in radiology reports measured 100 randomly selected reports, as in previous research.
answer_4.guideline: We used three human evaluation metrics for the JLiverCT dataset: correctness, fluency, and content order metrics. Only correctness and fluency are used for the MIMIC-CXR dataset because of the time series irrelevant scenario. Correctness measures how well a report describes its clinical information. The fluency score evaluates the naturalness of the generated reports with a 5-point Likert scale. Annotators extract the positions of descriptions regarding any finding labels in the gold report and the generated report; then, these positions are used to calculate the normalized Damerau-Levenshtein Distance to obtain the content order score.
